data_source: SYNTHETIC — generated by data/generate_books.py, seed 20260914. Not Presage data. Not customer data.
method: Readiness screen (7 checks) then a T-learner uplift baseline built from two logistic regressions.

books.how_contact_was_decided: Campaigns were sent to a random 80% of the book. A 20% holdout was deliberately left untouched so the team could measure lift.

readiness.verdict_summary: Contact varied close to independently of the customer, so this history supports a credible estimate across the book.

checks.name: Volume
checks.headline: 12,000 customers · 9,588 contacted / 2,412 not contacted
checks.detail: Presage's published floor is 1,000 recurring customers. This book holds 12,000, with a median of 177 behavioural events per customer. The number that actually constrains the analysis is the smaller arm: 2,412 customers.
checks.remedy: Extend the export window, or include cancelled customers who were active during the period.

checks.name: History depth and outcome window
checks.headline: 3.2 years of book history · 0.0% of outcomes unfinished
checks.detail: The CRM holds 3.2 years of records, clearing Presage's two-year floor. Within that, the median customer has 21 months of their own history and 7% have under six months, which is short for a stable baseline. Separately, 0.0% of customers have not yet completed the 180-day outcome window, so whether they stayed is not yet known. Counting an unfinished window as 'retained' would quietly bias the result upward.
checks.remedy: Exclude customers whose outcome window has not closed, or take the snapshot far enough in the past that it has.

checks.name: Treatment variation
checks.headline: 79.9% of the book was contacted
checks.detail: A causal question needs both answers to exist in the history: some customers contacted, some left alone. Here 79.9% were contacted, leaving 2,412 untouched. If a company has contacted essentially everyone, there is no 'what would have happened otherwise' anywhere in the data, and no method recovers one.
checks.remedy: Identify any historical suppression list, bounce cohort or unsubscribed segment — these are accidental control groups. Otherwise a forward holdout is required.

checks.name: Overlap and positivity
checks.headline: Contact was 0.51 AUC predictable · 99.7% of the book has a comparison group
checks.detail: I fit a logistic regression to predict, from pre-contact features only, who was contacted. It reaches 0.51 AUC (0.50 = a coin flip, 1.00 = perfectly predictable). Contact looks close to random with respect to what was known about the customer. This history behaves like an experiment, which is the best case. Slicing that score into 20 bins and keeping only bins that hold at least 10 customers from each arm and at least 5% of the bin from each arm, 99.7% of this book sits in a region where a comparison is actually possible.
checks.remedy: Ask what rule or process drove historical sends. Then restrict the audit to the overlap region and say so, or start a randomised holdout and revisit.

checks.name: Covariate balance
checks.headline: Largest imbalance 0.06 on plan_tier__pro · 0 of 15 features above 0.10
checks.detail: For every feature I compared the contacted and not-contacted groups and expressed the gap in standard deviations. Below 0.10 the two groups look like the same population. The biggest gap here is 0.06 on 'plan_tier__pro'. Imbalance is not fatal on its own — it is what adjustment is for — but it tells you the raw difference in retention rates between the two groups is measuring the difference between the people, not the effect of contacting them.
checks.remedy: Nothing to request: this is a modelling consequence. It means an unadjusted comparison must not be reported, and adjustment must be shown alongside it.

checks.name: Temporal leakage
checks.headline: No post-treatment columns detected
checks.detail: Every column in this export is declared as measured in the baseline window that ends on the decision date, and no single column predicts the outcome strongly enough on its own to suggest an undeclared post-treatment field slipped in.
checks.remedy: Ask the customer to state, per column, the window it is measured over relative to the send. Drop anything measured after it.

checks.name: Statistical power
checks.headline: Smallest detectable uplift 2.0 pp · breakeven is 5.0 pp
checks.detail: Within the 11,964 customers that survive the overlap check (9,559 contacted, 2,405 not), and at a base retention rate of 88.6%, the smallest uplift detectable at 80% power is 2.0 pp. A contact costs €12 against a retained customer worth €240, so contact pays for itself above 5.0 pp. The detectable effect is smaller than the effect that matters, so the audit can tell those two apart.
checks.remedy: More customers in the smaller arm, a longer export window, or accept a narrower claim on a subgroup where power is adequate.

churn_risk.description: Contact the 702 customers with the highest in-house churn score — the same budget as the uplift policy, aimed by risk instead of by effect.

uplift.description: Contact only customers whose estimated uplift clears the 5% breakeven.

checks.name: Temporal leakage
checks.headline: 1 post-treatment column present in the export
checks.detail: The export contains save_offer_redeemed, which the schema marks as measured AFTER the contact decision. A column like that is a consequence of the treatment, not a cause of the outcome — you can only redeem a save offer if you were sent one. Left in a model it produces excellent accuracy and a worthless estimate.
checks.remedy: Ask the customer to state, per column, the window it is measured over relative to the send. Drop anything measured after it.

checks.name: Statistical power
checks.headline: Smallest detectable uplift 14.0 pp · breakeven is 5.0 pp
checks.detail: Within the 105 customers that survive the overlap check (64 contacted, 41 not), and at a base retention rate of 93.3%, the smallest uplift detectable at 80% power is 14.0 pp. A contact costs €12 against a retained customer worth €240, so contact pays for itself above 5.0 pp. The effect that matters is smaller than what this data can detect, so the audit cannot distinguish 'worth contacting' from 'not worth contacting'. A euro figure here would be noise.
checks.remedy: More customers in the smaller arm, a longer export window, or accept a narrower claim on a subgroup where power is adequate.
